Bug_Title: IM: Integer multiply of result of integer remainder (IM_MULTIPLYING_RESULT_OF_IREM)
Bug_Details:
The code multiplies the result of an integer remaining by an integer constant.
Be sure you don't have your operator precedence confused. For example
i % 60 * 1000 is (i % 60) * 1000, not i % (60 * 1000).
Bug_Explanation: The code multiplies the result of an integer remainder by an integer constant. In this case, the bug is on line 5 where 'i % 60 * 1000' is being calculated. This is different from '(i % 60) * 1000', because operator precedence means 'i % 60' is done first before '*' is done.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case must fail because the bug in the original code multiplies the result of the integer remainder (i % 60) by 1000, not the remainder itself. Therefore, the expected result should be 4000, but it will be different as per the code (8000), which is not the expected result. The test case is designed to fail with this input.
